IncidentBot: :rotating_light: HIGH latency spike detected for continuous-batching pool 'cb-prod-us-west-2' - p95 increased to 820ms, queue depth 12,400, microbatch backlog rising. Pager: @oncall-Miguel. Incident ID: CB-2026-03-15-01
Alice R: seeing customer 500s + big throughput drop on hosted text/generate. Started ~03:42 UTC. KV cache miss rate jumped from ~3% to ~45% and per-shard mem usage spiked. Could be cache blowup or bad batch sizing.
Miguel: on it. pulling dashboards now (latency, qlen, microbatch size distribution). Any recent rollouts?
Alice R: Not from me. Config snapshot from the affected pool:```json
{
  "continuous_batching":{
    "microbatch_max":32,
    "microbatch_target":16,
    "jitter_ms":2,
    "kv_cache_max_entries":100000,
    "kv_cache_eviction_policy":"lru"
  }
}```
Samir: I did a canary quantization change ~30m ago but it was strictly canary, no prod traffic. No other infra changes.
Miguel: OK. hypothesis: at high concurrency, low jitter + large microbatch_max causes synchronized microbatches -> bursty memory pressure -> KV cache thrash. Quick mitigation plan: 1) bump jitter to 15ms 2) lower microbatch_max to 12 3) reduce kv_cache_max_entries to force earlier eviction 4) route 10% traffic to model-variant-slow as fallback. I'll push a hotfix now.
Miguel: running hotfix commands:```bash
# increase jitter, reduce microbatch size, drop cache entries
redwoodctl rollout update pool cb-prod-us-west-2 --set continuous_batching.jitter_ms=15 --set continuous_batching.microbatch_max=12 --set continuous_batching.kv_cache_max_entries=60000 --reason "hotfix: mitigate cb perf cliff"
redwoodctl traffic split set cb-prod-us-west-2 --variant model-variant-slow --percent 10
```
ops-bot: rollout started for pool cb-prod-us-west-2 by Miguel. change-id: rdu-187201-01.
ops-bot: rollout step: update config on 6 nodes.
ops-bot: rollout complete, status=SUCCESS, change-id=rdu-187201-01.
Miguel: changes applied. watching metrics.
Alice R: metrics 90s after hotfix: p95 down from 820ms -> 240ms, queue depth 12.4k -> 1.3k, microbatch distribution tightened, KV cache miss rate down to 12%. Throughput recovered to ~95% baseline.
Samir: nice. :thumbsup: Can you snapshot logs around eviction churn?
Miguel: grabbing logs. key excerpt:```
[03:42:12] shard-7 evict count spike: +124k entries in 60s
[03:42:14] mem.used=86% -> garbage collect triggered
[03:42:17] microbatch flush alignment across 1280 workers -> heavy I/O
[03:44:05] post-hotfix jitter=15ms -> microbatch offsets de-synchronized, evict rate normalized
```
Jen K: I'll take customer comms. Which customers were impacted? rough list/names and recommended note?
Alice R: We see error spikes for three top-level accounts on us-west: acme-inc, hyperstack, mailify. Errors peaked 03:42-03:46 UTC. Suggest: short incident note, acknowledge degraded performance, say mitigated by config hotfix, we are doing root cause analysis and follow-up with timeline + credits offer.
Miguel: initial RCA hypothesis: continuous batching scheduler experienced microbatch alignment at high concurrency because jitter_ms was set too low. Large microbatch_max (32) allowed big working sets that caused KV cache churn; combined with spike in concurrent input prefixes caused cache blowup and eviction storms. The hotfix reduced synchronization (jitter->15ms) and reduced batch size so fewer unique keys per batch, plus temporary routing to slower variant to reduce peak working set.
Samir: I'll also roll back the canary quant change from earlier (to be safe) and run a controlled perf test.
Miguel: rollback canary noted. I'll open a follow-up issue for longer-term fixes: auto-tune jitter by concurrency, per-pool microbatch caps, smarter KV admission (pin hot keys), and add circuit for backpressure before cache thrash.
Alice R: handing to Jen for comms, Samir for follow-up perf tests, Miguel for postmortem write. I will create incident ticket and link traces.
IncidentBot: Incident CB-2026-03-15-01 severity set to SEV2. Paging cleared.
Jen K: drafting outbound now. Will ping legal/CS for account-specific language.
Samir: small suggestion — add a proactive alert: "kv_cache_eviction_rate > 50k/min AND p95 > 500ms" to catch next-class of blowups earlier.
Miguel: agree. Also schedule a canary test that ramps concurrency while measuring microbatch alignment stats.
Alice R: confirmed recovery stable for 10m. closing active mitigation. I'll file followup postmortem and link timelines, graphs, and config diffs.
Jen K: customers notified with apology + 10% credits offer; two asked for a technical summary — I'll collect the postmortem once ready.
Samir: thanks team. I'll coordinate perf tests and add a reproducer to the infra repo.
Miguel: thx all. handoff complete — assigning to eng-sre for deep RCA and to product for follow-up controls.
Alice R: adding to ops board: CARD-4576 "continuous-batching: auto-jitter tuning + microbatch hard cap".
Jen K: will join postmortem meeting at 10:00 UTC.
Miguel: closing thread, will post RCA draft in #postmortems when done.
